notes: Human product review confirmed that API tokens are used for API access, while username and password are used to log in through the UI. The production answer correctly described API-token authentication; the machine failure was caused by literal expected wording.
Human product review confirmed the answer is correct. It identifies POST /api/tokens/authenticate and the API-token Authorization header without adding unnecessary scope.
Human product review confirmed case 3 is correct and appropriately scoped.
Human product review confirmed case 4 is correct and appropriately scoped.

Human product review confirmed that user access tokens do not expire, but a user can delete or regenerate them, and tokens associated with an account should no longer be valid if the owning user loses access. The production answer conveyed these conditions; the machine failure was caused by literal wording.

Human product review confirmed that tokens associated with an inactivated user should no longer work. The production answer correctly stated that the tokens are invalidated; the exact-string scorer failed on wording. Human also proposed a future runtime test using a newly created test user and token, followed by inactivation from the original administrator account and a rejected authentication attempt. That runtime test is captured separately and was not executed.

Human product review confirmed that one user can have multiple tokens and that duplicate token names are allowed; the UI does not warn that a name is already in use, so duplicate names merely make tokens harder to track. The production answer incorrectly claimed names must be unique, although that claim faithfully matches the pinned 2026.7 documentation. Preserve the baseline and treat this as a corpus-correctness/benchmark revision candidate until version-matched behavior is confirmed.

Human product review confirmed the answer is correct: a token value is shown only at creation and cannot be viewed later; regeneration replaces the previous value. The machine failed because it expected the literal phrase 'cannot view the value'.

Human product review confirmed the accurate current path is User menu -> Access Tokens -> + Create Token. The production answer surfaced that path but incorrectly selected User menu -> My Access Tokens -> Create New Token as its primary recommendation. The machine passed an answer whose final guidance was wrong.

Human product review found the fact technically correct but too vague for a new customer. The answer should explain that a project is the top-level container for an application or product, holds one or more project versions, and that scans/BOMs are associated with those versions.

The answer came directly from the pinned 2026.7 creating-a-project documentation, which states that projects or applications are limited to 10GB of Managed Code base. Human reviewer is unsure whether this is currently true or what Managed Code base includes. The corpus does not establish enforcement scope, licensing dependence, scan-type applicability, or behavior on the 2026.4 shared instance; do not promote this as a universal product claim without further product-expert or version-matched evidence.

Human product review confirmed that project names must be unique within the Black Duck instance and accepted the Detect duplicate-project exit-code detail as useful context. The reviewer believes an existing name may overwrite the project, but that behavior is unverified; the pinned documentation and current answer describe a uniqueness conflict rather than overwrite. Keep overwrite behavior unresolved until version-matched evidence is available.

Human product review confirmed that a newly created Black Duck SCA project starts with one version and can have additional versions added later. Additional product context: the default maximum is 10 project versions, visible under System settings -> Product Registration, with case-by-case account-team/licensing review required for exceptions. The pinned corpus does not currently contain this policy, so it is captured separately as an unverified candidate. The machine failure was caused by literal wording.

The default phase is In Planning, but the customer-facing answer should also explain that the user is expected to select the phase appropriate to the version's lifecycle; stating only the default is incomplete guidance.

Human review confirms the six phases and archived-risk distinction for the 2026.7 documentation answer. Test environment is Black Duck SCA 2026.4, where Archived is already deprecated. Version-specific guidance must account for that difference.

External is the documented default, but customer guidance should explain that the customer must select the appropriate distribution from the four available options based on the codebase and its context. Default-only wording is incomplete.

Documentation appears to support excluding Internal distributions from aggregate project risk calculations, but reviewer requests product-expert confirmation. Related unresolved migration question: what happens to historically Archived versions when upgrading to a SCA version where the Archived phase is deprecated? Do not infer behavior without version-specific upgrade evidence.
Correct. Even though Archived is deprecated in the 2026.4 test environment, archived versions are not included in project risk calculations.
Human review confirms that new policy rules and changes to existing policy expressions are not evaluated for Archived versions, while violations from disabled or deleted rules are removed.

The documentation says a clone of an Archived source version defaults to In Development, but human review requested runtime verification. An approval-gated candidate will create and scan an isolated version, make a documented BOM edit, clone it, rescan the same source into the clone, and record both the clone phase and whether the manual BOM edit is retained, overwritten, or transformed.
Human review confirms individual component or remediation values cannot be cloned. Cloning occurs at the project-version level; category-level clone options do not select individual values.
Human review confirms LTS conversion is one-way and cannot be reverted to Active; the warning about removed project and scan data is appropriate.
Human review confirms all components and subprojects in the project-version BOM are included by default unless explicitly excluded.
Human review confirms the 10-attempt threshold, 10-minute lockout, reset behavior, and exclusion of SAML/LDAP users.
Human review confirms the built-in failed-password lockout does not apply to SAML or LDAP users; their identity provider or directory may enforce separate policies.
Human review confirms the default local-account password requirements: eight characters and one required character type; LDAP/SAML accounts are excluded.
Accepted as correct based on the cited documentation stating a 128-character maximum. Runtime enforcement has not been independently tested.
Human review confirms Global Project Administrator, Global Project Manager, and Project Creator; Project Creator is limited to projects created by that user.
Human review confirms the Global Release Creator role has Create permission only for project versions and cannot edit or delete them.
